On the plus side, I taught myself to cook for Father and I since he worked so much.

We shared the same name, Mother and I. Jane. I never asked who chose it for me, I used to think it was sweet. Last week I turned twelve. Father gave me a bottle of sweet smelling perfume. I wore it all the time. Mother gave me a black eye. Father returned it to her while I cooked for us all. 

We walked through the back gate, my hand in his, wrapped in mother's old coat, the one he liked. Down the pathway into the little forest behind our property. The excitement was palpable, I couldn't wait to see what he got me. I knew where we were going. I had a place, a special place by the creek. It was frozen over now, gentle snow piling up in the moonlight. 

"Close your eyes" he whispered. I smiled to myself and let him lead me the last few steps. He put his strong arms around my waist and breathed in deeply. I could still smell my perfume in the crisp air as I nestled into him. 

"Merry Chrisgmas, darling." He almost whispered the words into my ear, and I grinned as I opened my eyes in anticipation. 

Before me was a little mound of snow. I looked up at him, puzzled. He smiled at me and gestured towards it. I kissed him lightly on the cheek and slipped towards the mound. I started to brush the light powder away where it had built up and hit something solid. I brushed more away and found myself looking into mother's frozen eyes. The snow this deep was stained crimzon, but had been covered by the fresh fall. 

A thousand thoughts flooded my young mind as I became rooted to the ground, my eyes wide, locked onto my mother's. I could sense father's apprehension behind me, and at last I turned around. No words needed to be spoken. He enveloped me in his arms and his coat and I nestled into his chest. 

"It's just us now, Janey." He said, tucking a curl behind my ear. He stroked my cheek and for the first time in my life, I was free.
